name: loneliness and making friends as an adult
description: A lonely person with no friends shares their state, asks how to make friends as an adult, and wonders why they have none. Verifies the friendship_lonely fact (micro interactions, shared-interest spaces, parallel play, patience) and that the disclosure itself routes to the loneliness topic with empathy.

turns.text: I have no friends and I feel lonely
How do I make friends as an adult?
Why do I have no friends?

expected.finalTurn: Turn 1: the lonely disclosure routes to the loneliness/feeling topics with a caring question. Turn 2: the how-to-make-friends question returns the friendship_lonely fact with small concrete steps. Turn 3: the why-do-I-have-none question stays on the loneliness thread.
expected.behavior: Loneliness is validated as common and unlinked to being unlovable. The fact offers low-pressure first steps (hellos, shared-interest groups, parallel activities) and points to a counselor when the feeling is heavy and long-lasting.
